_description: Outreach message templates. 4 pain buckets x 4 framing angles = 16 templates. Variables: {name}, {company}, {title}, {signal}, {metric}.

direct.hook: {name}, {company} ships {metric} PRs a week. How many get real scrutiny?
direct.pain: When PR volume outpaces review capacity, the review that happens becomes a rubber stamp. The checkbox exists. The evidence doesn't.
direct.value: We built a free GitHub Action that risk-classifies every PR proportionally. Typo fix gets waved through. Auth change gets a 3-model council review. Evidence bundle on every merge.
direct.cta: Want me to run it on one of your repos? Takes 2 minutes to install.

compliance.hook: {name}, when your auditor asks how {company} governed {metric} PRs last quarter, what do you show them?
compliance.pain: SOC 2 asks for evidence of review. Not that review happened -- that it was proportional to risk. Most teams can't reconstruct that story.
compliance.value: codeguard-action produces a signed evidence bundle on every PR. Risk tier, reviewer consensus, hash-chained audit trail. Free, open source.
compliance.cta: I can show you what a governed PR trail looks like in 10 minutes.

platform.hook: {name}, a free GitHub Action that risk-classifies every PR and produces evidence bundles.
platform.pain: Most governance tools treat every change the same. That's why developers hate them. Proportional review means typo fixes flow and auth changes get scrutiny.
platform.value: codeguard-action: risk tiers L0-L4, AI review council, evidence bundles. Install in your CI pipeline in 2 minutes.

consultant.hook: {name}, a free PR governance action you can install on client repos.
consultant.pain: When you tell a client their code review process has gaps, you need evidence. Not opinions -- evidence.
consultant.value: codeguard-action produces signed evidence bundles on every PR. Install on a client repo, show them the governance gap report. Makes your compliance work defensible.
consultant.cta: Want me to walk you through a client deployment?

direct.hook: {name}, your team approved {metric} PRs last month. Can you prove any of them were actually reviewed?
direct.pain: Approval happened. Evidence didn't. That's the gap between code review and code governance.
direct.value: codeguard-action generates a cryptographic evidence bundle on every PR. Who reviewed, what they found, what the risk tier was, and whether consensus was reached.
direct.cta: Can I run our action on one of your public repos and show you what it finds?

compliance.hook: {name}, approved is not governed. Your auditor knows the difference.
compliance.pain: SOC 2 evidence requests don't ask 'did someone click approve.' They ask 'can you prove the review was adequate for the risk level of the change.'
compliance.value: codeguard-action classifies risk, runs proportional AI review, and produces hash-chained evidence bundles. Audit-ready, free, open source.
compliance.cta: I can show you what audit-ready evidence looks like for {company}'s workflow.

platform.hook: GitHub tells you what changed. GuardSpine tells you what it means that it changed.
platform.pain: Your CI pipeline catches build failures. It doesn't catch governance failures. A PR that passes tests but modifies auth logic without evidence of review is a governance gap.
platform.value: codeguard-action: adds governance evidence to your existing CI pipeline. Risk classification, AI review, signed bundles. 2-minute install.
platform.cta: github.com/DNYoussef/codeguard-action -- try it on one repo.

consultant.hook: {name}, evidence bundles make your compliance deliverables concrete instead of opinion-based.
consultant.pain: When a client asks 'how do we know our code review process is adequate,' you need something better than 'we checked the PR approvals.'
consultant.value: codeguard-action gives you per-PR evidence: risk tier, review depth, consensus score, hash chain. Install on client repos, export the bundles, attach to your assessment.
consultant.cta: Want to see what a client evidence report looks like?

direct.hook: {name}, does {company} treat a typo fix the same as an auth change? Most teams do.
direct.pain: That's not governance. That's a checkbox. Governance means the risky changes get more scrutiny than the routine ones.
direct.value: codeguard-action classifies every PR into risk tiers. L0 trivial changes auto-pass. L3 security changes get a 3-model AI council. Proportional, not uniform.
direct.cta: Want to walk through one repo together?

compliance.hook: {name}, proportional review isn't optional anymore. Auditors are starting to ask for it.
compliance.pain: Treating every PR the same is actually a compliance risk. It means your high-risk changes got the same 30-second glance as a README update.
compliance.value: codeguard-action classifies risk and reviews proportionally. The evidence bundle proves the review depth matched the risk level.
compliance.cta: I can map where your current review process has evidence gaps.

platform.hook: Risk-tiered PR governance as a GitHub Action. L0 auto-pass to L4 human approval.
platform.pain: Most security tools have one mode: block or allow. Real governance is proportional. Different risk levels need different review depths.
platform.value: codeguard-action: 5 risk tiers, pattern-based + AI classification, multi-model review council, evidence bundles. Free.

consultant.hook: {name}, help your clients implement proportional code governance without slowing their teams.
consultant.pain: Clients push back on governance tools because they slow everything down equally. Proportional review fixes that -- routine changes flow, risky changes get depth.
consultant.value: Free GitHub Action. Install on client repos. Show them the risk distribution. Then have the conversation about what proportional governance looks like for them.
consultant.cta: Want me to walk you through a client setup?

direct.hook: {name}, if an auditor asked {company} to reconstruct the review trail for last Tuesday's deploy, how long would it take?
direct.pain: If the answer is 'more than 5 minutes,' you have a regulatory readiness gap. The evidence exists somewhere -- but can you find it, correlate it, and present it under pressure?
direct.value: codeguard-action produces structured evidence bundles on every PR. Risk tier, reviewer consensus, findings, hash chain. Searchable. Exportable. Audit-ready.
direct.cta: Can I show you what an evidence walkthrough looks like?

compliance.hook: {name}, SOC 2 Type II wants continuous evidence, not point-in-time. How does {company} generate that for code changes?
compliance.pain: Point-in-time audits are becoming continuous monitoring requirements. If your evidence is manual screenshots of PR approvals, you're building on sand.
compliance.value: codeguard-action generates structured, hash-chained evidence bundles on every PR automatically. Continuous. Machine-readable. Audit-ready.
compliance.cta: I can show you what continuous code governance evidence looks like in 10 minutes.

platform.hook: Continuous code governance evidence as a GitHub Action.
platform.pain: Compliance teams want evidence. Engineering teams want velocity. The answer isn't choosing one -- it's proportional governance that gives both.
platform.value: codeguard-action: automatic risk classification + proportional review + evidence bundles on every merge. Free, open source, 2-minute install.

consultant.hook: {name}, continuous governance evidence for your regulated clients. Free tool, zero vendor lock-in.
consultant.pain: Your regulated clients need evidence of code governance between audits, not just at audit time. Manual processes don't scale.
consultant.value: codeguard-action generates evidence bundles on every PR automatically. Install on client repos, export bundles into your compliance reports. Makes your deliverables concrete.
consultant.cta: Want to see a client evidence report?

classification_rules._description: Rule-based pain bucket classification. No LLM needed.

angle_selection_rules._description: Select framing angle by prospect lane/persona.
